tip: Assign squads to number keys so panic never leaves your archers standing in front.
Spacebar freezes time; use it to think before your front line turns into expensive meat.
Hold position keeps pikemen planted instead of chasing one dying goblin into an ambush.
Mercenaries fight for coin, not poetry—keep gold in reserve before hiring replacements.
Area spells scorch friend and foe alike; aim past your own shield-wall, not onto it.
Rotate the camera near cliffs and ruined walls; ambushers love blind angles.
Thornvael caches your campaign locally—progress saves safely even if your connection drops.
Save manually before entering unfamiliar ruins; overconfidence leaves no corpses to loot.
Wedge formations punch through thin lines; box formations keep fragile mages breathing.
A dead mage casts zero spells; spend a few coins on robes and charms before glory.
Potions belong on quick-slots, not buried at the bottom of a pack during a charge.
Flanking strikes bypass shields; pin enemies with warriors, then circle with blades.
High ground extends bow range and accuracy—seize ridges before trading volleys.
Selling rusted scrap in town pays for bandages; leaving it in mud pays nothing.
Check merchants after every major battle; caravans bring fresh stock with new rumors.
Focus fire drops dangerous hexers fast; wounded enemies still swing at full strength.
Control groups remember your roster across missions—rebind after hiring fresh blood.
Tomes teach permanent spells; scrolls burn to ash after a single desperate reading.
Mana regenerates faster out of combat—pause advancing until your casters recover.
Heavy plate slows marching speed; don't let swift scouts outrun their own rescue.
Click the minimap to jump across wide battlefields faster than scrolling through fog.
Side trails hide supply caches and old graves—both worth more than an empty road.
Heroes carry the banner; if yours falls, the company breaks no matter who survives.
Inspect rare gear carefully—some relics carry history that hints at stronger sets.
Thornwick's bridge tolls are highway robbery, yet cheaper than swimming in chain mail.
Border Fords raiders strike supply wagons first; guard your flanks on narrow roads.
Fen fog hides archers until ten paces—send a shielded scout ahead of your casters.
Lightning spells arc violently in wet weather and shallow river fords.
In Redmarsh, standing water slows heavy boots—lure foes onto dry hummocks first.
Poison clouds linger in windless hollows; pull your squad back instead of choking.
Redmarsh apothecaries charge double for healing draughts—stock up before leaving town.
Broken wardstones distort spell ranges; watch your casters' footing near violet rifts.
Oakhaven's tower guild buys rare scrolls at fair rates—if you survive the road there.
Coastal gales scatter loose formations; tighten ranks before crossing sea cliffs.
Frost magic freezes slick cobbles and tidal causeways, slowing charging cavalry.
Iron Coast raiders favor heavy arbalests—keep tower shields raised while closing.
Ironcamp smiths forge the finest plate in the realm, priced for men expecting to die.
Ember Court hexers weaken your strongest warrior first—carry Ward Charms into battle.
Obsidian trenches punish bunched squads; split into two groups to clear crossfire.
Fire resistance saves lives in the Crownlands—swap rings before marching into ash.
Yes, you can hoard ninety healing potions until the credits roll. No, they won't help.
Retreating to regroup costs pride; wiping out costs your entire save file's dignity.
Every mercenary claims to be a veteran until the first fireball lands near their boots.
Offline play works seamlessly—Thornvael needs no royal courier watching every click.
If a bridge looks suspiciously unguarded, congratulations: you found the ambush.
Two-handed swords clear crowds fast, provided someone else is catching the arrows.
Stilettos and rondels shine against armored captains once their shield-arm is tied up.
Check your squad's health bars after every skirmish—bleeding out between fights is bad form.
Summoned storms don't care who paid for the tome; keep casters clear of the eye.
Repairing and upgrading equipment in towns beats praying to headless statues on the road.
Scout ahead with swift units, then pull back to your prepared kill-zone.
Rings and amulets weigh nothing—leaving slots empty is voluntary suffering.
A single well-timed Stone Curse stops a charging berserker colder than a speech.
Archers auto-target nearby threats unless ordered to focus enemy healers.
Fog of war hides terrain hazards as well as foes—watch where your boots step.
Gold weighs nothing in your purse until a merchant sees how much you're carrying.
Crowd control wins outnumbered fights; damage alone just trades bodies faster.
Double-click a unit type to select every matching fighter currently on screen.
The Ember Court remembers every mercy you showed—usually by trying to exploit it.
When all else fails, pause, breathe, and check if your healer still has mana.
Spread your company out when facing enemy artillery or fireball casters so one blast cannot cripple everyone.
Wedge formation punches cleanly through chokepoints, while line formation prevents flanking on open ground.
Keep one fast melee fighter in reserve to peel hounds and stalkers off your backline healers.
Double-tapping a control group key centers your camera immediately on that squad's banner.
Never march your entire column down a narrow bridge without scouting the far bank first.
Boardwalks in Redmarsh force single-file columns; keep shield-bearers at both ends of your line.
Coastal cliff paths punish wide formations—group your archers on rocky ledges above the surf.
Against Cinder Citadel halberdiers, anchor your flanks against ruined walls to deny rear strikes.
Flanking an enemy from behind bypasses their shield block chance and deals bonus physical damage.
Stunning or knocking back a caster interrupts long ritual chants before the spell finishes.
High ground extends bow and spell range while penalizing the accuracy of foes shooting uphill.
Heavy armor slows movement and drains stamina faster; swap to lighter gear for long flanking marches.
Briar-hounds telegraph their lunge with a low crouch—step back or raise shields before they leap.
Plague-toads burst in a cloud of venom upon death; finish them with arrows rather than greataxes.
Barnacle-hulks shrug off glancing sword blows—bring maces, warhammers, or armor-piercing bolts.
Pyre-knights ignite nearby tiles when struck in melee; keep a water draught or frost spell handy.
Chilled targets swing slower and move sluggishly, buying precious seconds for your archers to reload.
Lightning spells arc farther across wet mud, shallow fords, and salt-soaked coastal stone.
Save single-use scrolls for boss phases or unexpected ambushes when your mage's mana runs dry.
Necromancers can detonate enemy corpses to break tightly packed enemy shield walls.
Fire spells ignite dry reeds along the Border Fords, creating brief walls of smoke and flame.
Marsh-gas pockets in Redmarsh detonate violently if struck by even the smallest spark bolt.
Storm charms and lightning wards drastically cut damage from Iron Coast tide-priests.
Frost magic cools molten slag-golems, briefly cracking their hardened obsidian shells.
Always keep enough coin for two days of mercenary wages before buying luxury unique gear.
Town blacksmiths pay better coin for intact armor than muddy, blood-stained rags.
Check tavern rumors before departing; an optional side-stash often pays for an entire expedition.
Selling unused scrolls and elixirs early funds the whetstones and healing draughts you actually need.
Thornwick merchants charge less for hemp rope and rations than quartermasters deeper in the fens.
Apothecaries in Redmarsh pay a premium for harvested toad-glands and intact wisp-lanterns.
Salvaged brass astrolabes and naval pay-boxes fetch top silver from Ironcamp harbor brokers.
Royal paper scrip loses value near the capital—insist on hard silver and bullion in Oakhaven.
Optional ruins and wayshrines often hide permanent stat charms behind simple environmental puzzles.
Listen closely to ambient sound; creaking leather and clinking mail betray hidden ambushes.
Inspecting landmarks unlocks regional lore entries and occasionally reveals hidden supply caches.
Dead-end paths along riverbanks and cliff edges frequently conceal smugglers' lockboxes.
Follow white-painted milestone posts to find safe shallow crossings across the Border Fords.
Glowing green lanterns off the Redmarsh dikes rarely lead to shelter—keep your steel drawn.
Low tide exposes hidden sea-caves and wrecked galley holds along the southern Iron Coast.
Deep gray ash drifts in Crown and Ember often conceal collapsed cellar grates and lost strongboxes.
The First Border Compact was signed in river-clay and iron, yet broken the moment silver ran scarce.
Sellswords in Thornvael rarely die of old age; most retire to a shallow ditch with unpaid wages.
Every royal tax-ledger in the capital weighs more in blood than in parchment.
Old veterans say the land itself remembers every oath sworn over cold steel.
Thornwick's granaries once fed three provinces before river-tariffs strangled the barge trade.
Redmarsh was dry farmland a century ago until the old river dikes were sabotaged during the First Rising.
Ironcamp's sea-wall was built from ballast stones dumped by merchant galleys that never returned.
The Cinder Throne earned its name when the First King burned his own siege-towers after taking the gate.
A surviving mercenary levels up and gains tougher traits; losing veterans hurts worse than losing gold.
Equip your hired shield-bearers with spare iron bucklers and greaves before marching into heavy fights.
Low morale makes wounded mercenaries waver; keep your hero close to rally faltering ranks.
Mix melee blockers with ranged crossbows so your company can adapt to both charges and kiting foes.
Thornwick tavern recruits come cheap, though most have never seen anything fiercer than a river-rat.
Fenland guides hired in Redmarsh ignore mud movement penalties and spot hidden bog-traps early.
Former galley-oarsmen recruited in Ironcamp excel at breaking shields with heavy boarding axes.
Disgraced royal deserters in Oakhaven demand steep coin, yet bring heavy plate and siege discipline.
Salvaging duplicate common weapons yields iron ingots and leather scraps for upgrading trusted gear.
Applying whetstones before a major mission grants a temporary edge bonus to all melee blades.
Combining minor resistance charms at an apothecary bench creates stronger multi-element wards.
Reinforcing leather armor with boiled hide plates boosts defense without slowing dodge recovery.
Bog-smelted ore from Redbank pits makes sturdy early arrowheads and replacement shield bosses.
Bitter-root salves brewed at Redmarsh campfires cure swamp-ague before it drains max stamina.
Whale-oil coatings crafted in Ironcamp prevent sea-spray from corroding steel armor ratings.
Mica-lined plating forged in Oakhaven insulates heavy armor against crown-fire and slag-golems.
Pause frequently during chaotic multi-front skirmishes to reassign targets and drink draughts.
Poison damage bypasses regular armor; rely on antidote vials and high poison resistance in wet regions.
Unstable rifts reward bold companies with rare set pieces, provided you clear surrounding patrols first.
A well-timed tactical retreat preserves your veteran roster when an elite boss catches you unprepared.
Necromancer minions draw enemy aggro away from fragile mages without costing a single copper in wages.
Repairing dented armor at town smithies restores full block and mitigation values before hard marches.
Border toll-collectors always hide their real silver beneath false bottoms in overturned chests.
Never camp beside stagnant red water without posting a sentry against night-creeping rot-hounds.
Corsair captains carry signal-horns; silence them first before they summon reinforcements from the coves.
The Sovereign's Inquisitors burned half the realm's ledgers to hide how deeply the Crown was in debt.
Stockpile Greater Healing Draughts in Oakhaven—the final approach to the throne offers few safe camps.
Completing a four-piece armor set unlocks powerful combat passives tailored to your hero's class.
Archers using heavy arbalests pierce thick plate easily, though they require protection while reloading.
Fire-ward charms sold by Oakhaven merchants are worth their weight in gold against pyre-knights.
Every fallen mercenary leaves a name on the company roll—lead wisely so the list stays short.
Smoke and ash reduce ranged accuracy in Act 4; push melee vanguards closer before loosing volleys.
